mapping.table_rationale: Patients is selected as the primary person table because demographic core fields (subject identifier, birth date components, sex) align cleanly and the majority of person-level attributes resolve there with high semantic overlap.

attributes.name: birth_datetime
attributes.rationale: The birth timestamp is taken directly from the dob column; it is the only field that stores a complete birth date and therefore supplies the required datetime value.

attributes.name: care_site_id
attributes.rationale: No persistent care-site identifier exists at the person level in MIMIC-III; any unit information is visit-scoped and cannot be attached to the static person record.

attributes.name: day_of_birth
attributes.rationale: Day component is extracted from the same dob date field that already holds the full birth date, making the derivation straightforward and reliable.

attributes.name: death_datetime
attributes.rationale: Date of death is stored in dod; the column is the canonical mortality field for the patient and maps one-to-one onto the OMOP death datetime.

attributes.name: ethnicity_concept_id
attributes.rationale: MIMIC-III records ethnicity only as free-text strings; no standardized concept identifier is present, so a concept_id mapping is impossible.

attributes.name: ethnicity_source_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Source concept identifiers for ethnicity are absent; the data model never stored coded ethnicity concepts.

attributes.name: ethnicity_source_value
attributes.rationale: Although ethnicity lives on the admission record rather than the static patient table, the free-text value is the only available source string and is therefore used.

attributes.name: gender_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Gender is stored as a simple coded value (M/F) in the patients table; the semantic match is exact and the confidence is correspondingly high.

attributes.name: gender_source_concept_id
attributes.rationale: No separate source-concept identifier exists for gender; the value is already the source itself.

attributes.name: gender_source_value
attributes.rationale: The same gender column supplies both the concept and the original source string, so the mapping re-uses that field.

attributes.name: location_id
attributes.rationale: Residential address information is not collected in MIMIC-III; consequently no location foreign key can be populated.

attributes.name: month_of_birth
attributes.rationale: Month is derived by extracting the month component of the dob date; the source column is unambiguous.

attributes.name: person_id
attributes.rationale: Subject_id is the primary key of the patients table and is used throughout MIMIC as the unique person identifier, giving a near-perfect match.

attributes.name: person_source_value
attributes.rationale: No additional external person identifier is stored; subject_id itself serves as both the internal and source value.

attributes.name: provider_id
attributes.rationale: Primary-care provider is not recorded on the static patient record; any caregiver links appear only in event tables.

attributes.name: race_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Race is not coded with OMOP concepts; the closest free-text field is ethnicity, which is insufficient for a concept_id.

attributes.name: race_source_concept_id
attributes.rationale: No race source-concept identifiers exist in the schema.

attributes.name: race_source_value
attributes.rationale: Ethnicity text is used as a weak proxy for race because MIMIC collapses the two concepts into a single free-text column; confidence is deliberately moderate.

attributes.name: year_of_birth
attributes.rationale: Year is obtained by extracting the year portion of dob; the column is the sole authoritative birth-date source.

mapping.table_rationale: Admissions is the natural home for visit_occurrence because each row represents a complete hospital stay with clear start and end timestamps and a unique hadm_id.

attributes.name: admitted_from_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Admission location is stored only as free text; no standardized concept identifier is available.

attributes.name: admitted_from_source_value
attributes.rationale: The free-text admission_location column directly answers the source-value requirement for the origin of the visit.

attributes.name: care_site_id
attributes.rationale: Care-site identifiers are not present on the admissions row; they would require joining to transfers.

attributes.name: discharge_to_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Discharge destination is never coded as a concept_id in MIMIC-III.

attributes.name: discharge_to_source_value
attributes.rationale: Discharge_location supplies the textual destination; the column was previously overlooked but is the correct source.

attributes.name: person_id
attributes.rationale: Subject_id on admissions is a foreign key to patients and therefore correctly links the visit to the person.

attributes.name: preceding_visit_occurrence_id
attributes.rationale: No explicit pointer to a prior admission is stored; any sequential relationship would have to be reconstructed.

attributes.name: provider_id
attributes.rationale: Admitting or attending provider is not recorded on the admissions table.

attributes.name: visit_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Visit type is free-text only; no OMOP visit concept is present.

attributes.name: visit_end_date
attributes.rationale: Dischtime provides the calendar date of discharge and is the definitive end-of-stay marker.

attributes.name: visit_end_datetime
attributes.rationale: The same dischtime column also carries the precise time component required for the datetime field.

attributes.name: visit_occurrence_id
attributes.rationale: Hadm_id is the unique hospital-admission identifier and maps directly onto visit_occurrence_id.

attributes.name: visit_source_concept_id
attributes.rationale: No source concept for visit type exists.

attributes.name: visit_source_value
attributes.rationale: Admission_type is the free-text classification of the visit and is therefore used as the source value.

attributes.name: visit_start_date
attributes.rationale: Admittime supplies the calendar start date of the hospital stay.

attributes.name: visit_start_datetime
attributes.rationale: The identical admittime column also contains the full timestamp needed for the datetime attribute.

attributes.name: visit_type_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Visit type remains uncoded; only the textual admission_type is available.

mapping.table_rationale: Transfers captures intra-hospital movements between care units and therefore supplies the finer-grained visit-detail grain that admissions cannot provide.

attributes.name: admitted_from_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Prior unit is recorded only as text or ward identifiers; no concept_id is present.

attributes.name: admitted_from_source_value
attributes.rationale: Prev_careunit is the textual origin of the transfer and is therefore chosen as the source value.

attributes.name: care_site_id
attributes.rationale: Curr_careunit identifies the current care unit and serves as a practical proxy for care_site_id.

attributes.name: discharge_to_concept_id
attributes.rationale: No coded discharge destination exists at the transfer level.

attributes.name: discharge_to_source_value
attributes.rationale: Next-unit information is not stored as a destination source value on the transfers row.

attributes.name: person_id
attributes.rationale: Subject_id links every transfer back to the patient, preserving the required person foreign key.

attributes.name: preceding_visit_detail_id
attributes.rationale: No explicit previous-transfer pointer is maintained in the schema.

attributes.name: provider_id
attributes.rationale: Provider information is absent from the transfers table.

attributes.name: visit_detail_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Transfer type is not coded with OMOP concepts.

attributes.name: visit_detail_end_date
attributes.rationale: Outtime marks the end of the unit stay and is therefore used for the end-date component.

attributes.name: visit_detail_end_datetime
attributes.rationale: The same outtime column supplies the precise end timestamp required by the datetime field.

attributes.name: visit_detail_id
attributes.rationale: Row_id on transfers provides a unique sequential identifier that can serve as visit_detail_id.

attributes.name: visit_detail_parent_id
attributes.rationale: No parent-detail hierarchy is modeled in the transfers table.

attributes.name: visit_detail_source_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Source concepts for transfer type do not exist.

attributes.name: visit_detail_source_value
attributes.rationale: Eventtype describes the nature of the transfer and is adopted as the source value.

attributes.name: visit_detail_start_date
attributes.rationale: Intime supplies the calendar start of the unit stay.

attributes.name: visit_detail_start_datetime
attributes.rationale: Intime also carries the full start timestamp needed for the datetime attribute.

attributes.name: visit_detail_type_concept_id
attributes.rationale: No type concept is recorded for transfers.

attributes.name: visit_occurrence_id
attributes.rationale: Hadm_id on the transfer links the detail back to the parent hospital admission.

mapping.table_rationale: Labevents is preferred over chartevents because it is the primary repository of laboratory specimens and their collection timestamps, even though the match remains only moderate.

attributes.name: anatomic_site_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Anatomic site is never coded as a concept in MIMIC laboratory tables.

attributes.name: anatomic_site_source_value
attributes.rationale: No free-text anatomic site is stored for laboratory specimens.

attributes.name: disease_status_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Disease-status concepts are outside the scope of the laboratory event tables.

attributes.name: disease_status_source_value
attributes.rationale: No disease-status source value is present.

attributes.name: person_id
attributes.rationale: Subject_id on labevents correctly references the patient who provided the specimen.

attributes.name: quantity
attributes.rationale: Specimen volume or quantity is not recorded.

attributes.name: specimen_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Specimen type is not standardized to OMOP concepts.

attributes.name: specimen_date
attributes.rationale: Charttime is the closest available collection timestamp and is therefore used for the specimen date.

attributes.name: specimen_datetime
attributes.rationale: The same charttime column supplies the full datetime of specimen collection.

attributes.name: specimen_id
attributes.rationale: Row_id provides a unique identifier that can stand in for specimen_id.

attributes.name: specimen_source_id
attributes.rationale: No external specimen source identifier exists.

attributes.name: specimen_source_value
attributes.rationale: Specimen source value is not captured as a distinct field.

attributes.name: specimen_type_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Type concepts are absent.

attributes.name: unit_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Unit concepts are not stored.

attributes.name: unit_source_value
attributes.rationale: Unit of the specimen itself is not recorded.

mapping.table_rationale: Labevents is the richest source of quantitative clinical measurements; the majority of value, unit and timing fields resolve there.

attributes.name: measurement_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Laboratory items are identified by free-text labels or itemids, never by OMOP concept identifiers.

attributes.name: measurement_date
attributes.rationale: Charttime supplies the date portion of the measurement event.

attributes.name: measurement_datetime
attributes.rationale: The identical charttime column also carries the precise time of the measurement.

attributes.name: measurement_id
attributes.rationale: Row_id is unique per laboratory result and therefore serves as measurement_id.

attributes.name: measurement_source_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Source concept identifiers are not present.

attributes.name: measurement_source_value
attributes.rationale: The label from the laboratory-item dictionary is the human-readable name of the measured analyte.

attributes.name: measurement_time
attributes.rationale: A pure time-of-day field is not stored separately from the full timestamp.

attributes.name: measurement_type_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Measurement type concepts are absent.

attributes.name: operator_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Comparison operators are not coded.

attributes.name: person_id
attributes.rationale: Subject_id correctly associates every laboratory result with the patient.

attributes.name: provider_id
attributes.rationale: Ordering or performing provider is not recorded on labevents.

attributes.name: range_high
attributes.rationale: Reference-range high values are not stored in the core tables.

attributes.name: range_low
attributes.rationale: Reference-range low values are likewise absent.

attributes.name: unit_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Units are free-text only.

attributes.name: unit_source_value
attributes.rationale: Valueuom holds the unit-of-measure string that accompanies the numeric result.

attributes.name: value_as_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Result values are never stored as concepts.

attributes.name: value_as_number
attributes.rationale: Valuenum is the numeric laboratory result and maps directly onto value_as_number.

attributes.name: value_source_value
attributes.rationale: The original textual representation of the result is preserved in the value column.

attributes.name: visit_detail_id
attributes.rationale: No visit-detail foreign key is present on labevents.

attributes.name: visit_occurrence_id
attributes.rationale: Hadm_id links the measurement to the enclosing hospital admission when available.

mapping.table_rationale: Procedures_icd is selected because it stores the coded procedure events; CPT events remain a secondary source.

attributes.name: modifier_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Procedure modifiers are not coded in MIMIC.

attributes.name: modifier_source_value
attributes.rationale: No free-text modifier field exists.

attributes.name: person_id
attributes.rationale: Subject_id associates each coded procedure with the correct patient.

attributes.name: procedure_concept_id
attributes.rationale: ICD procedure codes are not mapped to OMOP concepts inside the source tables.

attributes.name: procedure_date
attributes.rationale: No explicit procedure date column exists on procedures_icd; the table is essentially a diagnosis-style coding table.

attributes.name: procedure_datetime
attributes.rationale: When a timestamp is required, chartdate from the CPT events table is the closest available proxy.

attributes.name: procedure_occurrence_id
attributes.rationale: Row_id uniquely identifies each procedure coding record.

attributes.name: procedure_source_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Source concepts are not stored.

attributes.name: procedure_source_value
attributes.rationale: The ICD-9 procedure code itself is the canonical source value.

attributes.name: procedure_type_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Type concepts are absent.

attributes.name: provider_id
attributes.rationale: Performing provider is not linked on the procedure coding tables.

attributes.name: quantity
attributes.rationale: Quantity is not recorded for coded procedures.

attributes.name: visit_detail_id
attributes.rationale: No visit-detail link exists.

attributes.name: visit_occurrence_id
attributes.rationale: Hadm_id correctly places the procedure inside its hospital admission.

mapping.table_rationale: Diagnoses_icd is the dedicated diagnosis coding table and therefore a better fit for condition_occurrence than the admissions header.

attributes.name: condition_concept_id
attributes.rationale: ICD codes are not pre-mapped to OMOP condition concepts inside MIMIC.

attributes.name: condition_end_date
attributes.rationale: End-of-condition dates are not recorded on the diagnosis coding rows.

attributes.name: condition_end_datetime
attributes.rationale: No end datetime is available.

attributes.name: condition_occurrence_id
attributes.rationale: Row_id uniquely identifies each diagnosis coding instance.

attributes.name: condition_source_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Source concepts are absent.

attributes.name: condition_source_value
attributes.rationale: The ICD-9 diagnosis code is the definitive source value.

attributes.name: condition_start_date
attributes.rationale: Admission time is used as a proxy start date because diagnosis rows themselves carry no independent onset timestamp.

attributes.name: condition_start_datetime
attributes.rationale: The same admission timestamp supplies the start datetime when a more precise value is unavailable.

attributes.name: condition_status_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Condition status is not coded.

attributes.name: condition_status_source_value
attributes.rationale: No status source value exists.

attributes.name: condition_type_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Type concepts are missing.

attributes.name: person_id
attributes.rationale: Subject_id correctly links the diagnosis to the patient.

attributes.name: provider_id
attributes.rationale: Diagnosing provider is not recorded.

attributes.name: stop_reason
attributes.rationale: Stop reasons are outside the diagnosis coding model.

attributes.name: visit_detail_id
attributes.rationale: No visit-detail foreign key is present.

attributes.name: visit_occurrence_id
attributes.rationale: Hadm_id places the condition inside the correct hospital stay.

mapping.table_rationale: Although death is not a separate table, the patients table concentrates the essential mortality fields (dod, hospital_expire_flag) and is therefore adopted as the closest match.

attributes.name: cause_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Cause of death is never coded in MIMIC-III.

attributes.name: cause_source_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Source concepts for cause are absent.

attributes.name: cause_source_value
attributes.rationale: No free-text cause of death is stored.

attributes.name: death_date
attributes.rationale: Dod supplies the calendar date of death and is therefore mapped to death_date.

attributes.name: death_datetime
attributes.rationale: The same dod column also provides the timestamp component used for death_datetime.

attributes.name: death_type_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Death-type concepts are not present.

attributes.name: person_id
attributes.rationale: Subject_id is the natural person key for the death record.

mapping.table_rationale: MIMIC-III contains no residential or geographic address data; consequently no table can be assigned to the location entity.

attributes.name: address_1
attributes.rationale: Street address is never collected.

attributes.name: address_2
attributes.rationale: Secondary address line is absent.

attributes.name: city
attributes.rationale: City is not recorded.

attributes.name: county
attributes.rationale: County information is missing.

attributes.name: location_id
attributes.rationale: No location identifier exists.

attributes.name: location_source_value
attributes.rationale: No source value for location is available.

attributes.name: state
attributes.rationale: State is not stored.

attributes.name: zip
attributes.rationale: Postal code is absent.

mapping.table_rationale: Chartevents contains the bulk of free-text and numeric observational findings recorded during a stay and is therefore preferred over the admissions header for the observation entity.

attributes.name: obs_event_field_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Event-field concepts are not present.

attributes.name: observation_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Observations are identified by itemids, not by OMOP concepts.

attributes.name: observation_date
attributes.rationale: Charttime supplies the date of the recorded observation.

attributes.name: observation_datetime
attributes.rationale: The same column also carries the full timestamp.

attributes.name: observation_event_id
attributes.rationale: No separate event identifier is stored.

attributes.name: observation_id
attributes.rationale: Row_id uniquely identifies each charted observation.

attributes.name: observation_source_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Source concepts are absent.

attributes.name: observation_source_value
attributes.rationale: The item label from the dictionary is the readable source description of the observation.

attributes.name: observation_type_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Type concepts are not coded.

attributes.name: person_id
attributes.rationale: Subject_id correctly associates the observation with the patient.

attributes.name: provider_id
attributes.rationale: When a caregiver is recorded, cgid can be used as a provider surrogate.

attributes.name: qualifier_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Qualifiers are not standardized.

attributes.name: qualifier_source_value
attributes.rationale: No qualifier source value is stored.

attributes.name: unit_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Units remain free-text.

attributes.name: unit_source_value
attributes.rationale: Valueuom holds the unit string that accompanies numeric observations.

attributes.name: value_as_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Values are never stored as concepts.

attributes.name: value_as_datetime
attributes.rationale: Datetime-valued observations are rare and not specially flagged.

attributes.name: value_as_number
attributes.rationale: Valuenum is the numeric component of charted observations.

attributes.name: value_as_string
attributes.rationale: The original textual value is preserved in the value column.

attributes.name: visit_detail_id
attributes.rationale: No visit-detail link is present.

attributes.name: visit_occurrence_id
attributes.rationale: Hadm_id places the observation inside the correct admission.

mapping.table_rationale: MIMIC-III does not define continuous observation periods; only discrete admission intervals exist, so no table can be confidently assigned.

attributes.name: observation_period_end_date
attributes.rationale: No period-end field is defined.

attributes.name: observation_period_id
attributes.rationale: No period identifier exists.

attributes.name: observation_period_start_date
attributes.rationale: No period-start field is defined.

attributes.name: period_type_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Period-type concepts are absent.

attributes.name: person_id
attributes.rationale: No person link can be established for a non-existent period.

mapping.table_rationale: Prescriptions is the principal medication-order table and therefore the best match for drug_exposure, supplemented by input-event tables for administration detail.

attributes.name: days_supply
attributes.rationale: Days-of-supply is not calculated or stored.

attributes.name: dose_unit_source_value
attributes.rationale: Dose_unit_rx holds the unit of the prescribed dose and is therefore preferred.

attributes.name: drug_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Drug concepts are not pre-mapped.

attributes.name: drug_exposure_end_date
attributes.rationale: Enddate marks the intended end of the prescription.

attributes.name: drug_exposure_end_datetime
attributes.rationale: For infusions the more precise endtime from inputevents_mv is used when available.

attributes.name: drug_exposure_id
attributes.rationale: Row_id uniquely identifies each prescription record.

attributes.name: drug_exposure_start_date
attributes.rationale: Startdate is the official start of the medication order.

attributes.name: drug_exposure_start_datetime
attributes.rationale: The same startdate column supplies the datetime when a more granular start time is unavailable.

attributes.name: drug_source_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Source concepts are missing.

attributes.name: drug_source_value
attributes.rationale: The drug name string is the primary source value.

attributes.name: drug_type_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Type concepts are not recorded.

attributes.name: lot_number
attributes.rationale: Lot numbers are never captured.

attributes.name: person_id
attributes.rationale: Subject_id links the exposure to the patient.

attributes.name: provider_id
attributes.rationale: Ordering provider is not stored on the prescriptions table.

attributes.name: quantity
attributes.rationale: Dose_val_rx supplies the numeric quantity of the prescribed dose.

attributes.name: refills
attributes.rationale: Refill counts are not recorded.

attributes.name: route_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Route is free-text only.

attributes.name: route_source_value
attributes.rationale: The route column holds the administration route string.

attributes.name: sig
attributes.rationale: Sig (directions) text is not stored as a distinct field.

attributes.name: stop_reason
attributes.rationale: Statusdescription on the input-event tables often indicates why an infusion was stopped.

attributes.name: verbatim_end_date
attributes.rationale: No separate verbatim end date is maintained.

attributes.name: visit_detail_id
attributes.rationale: Visit-detail linkage is absent.

attributes.name: visit_occurrence_id
attributes.rationale: Hadm_id correctly situates the drug exposure inside the hospital admission.

mapping.table_rationale: MIMIC-III does not systematically record implantable or temporary medical devices; consequently no table can be mapped to device_exposure.

attributes.name: device_concept_id

attributes.name: device_exposure_end_date
attributes.rationale: No end-date field exists.

attributes.name: device_exposure_end_datetime

attributes.name: device_exposure_start_date

attributes.name: device_source_value

attributes.name: device_type_concept_id
attributes.rationale: Type concepts are absent.

attributes.name: person_id

attributes.name: provider_id
attributes.rationale: No provider link exists.

attributes.name: quantity
attributes.rationale: Quantity is not applicable.

attributes.name: unique_device_id
attributes.rationale: Unique device identifiers are never captured.

attributes.name: visit_detail_id
attributes.rationale: No visit-detail link exists.

mapping.table_rationale: Noteevents is the dedicated clinical-note repository and therefore the unambiguous match for the note entity.

attributes.name: language_concept_id

attributes.name: note_class_concept_id
